programs.name: ACCA
programs.tagline: A globally recognised accountancy qualification — from Foundation to Strategic Professional.
programs.description: The ACCA route starts with a short ladder of computer-based exams. You can enter at the level that matches your background, and no previous qualification is needed for the Intermediate Certificate or the Diploma. Students with no accounting background are advised to begin with FA1 and MA1.

overview.title: Foundations in Accountancy (FIA) and Knowledge level
paragraphs: The ACCA route starts with a short ladder of computer-based exams. You can enter at the level that matches your background, and no previous qualification is needed for the Intermediate Certificate or the Diploma. Students with no accounting background are advised to begin with FA1 and MA1.
bullets: Introductory Certificate in Financial and Management Accounting: FA1 and MA1
Intermediate Certificate in Financial and Management Accounting: FA2 and MA2
Diploma in Accounting and Business (FIA) and Applied Knowledge (ACCA Qualification): BT/FBT, MA/FMA and FA/FFA

overview.title: Applied Skills level
paragraphs: Applied Skills is the second level of the ACCA Qualification. It moves from objective tests to a mix of objective test questions and written or calculated answers. Corporate and Business Law (LW) is on demand, and the other five exams are held in four sessions a year. Students complete Applied Knowledge before Applied Skills.

overview.title: Strategic Professional level
paragraphs: Strategic Professional is the final exam level. Students complete two compulsory Essentials papers, SBL and SBR, and then choose Options papers. All exams are computer-based, use long scenario-based questions and are held in four sessions a year. Every exam awards professional skills marks for how well you analyse, communicate and use judgement.

levels.name: Foundation Level (FIA / Applied Knowledge)
levels.description: Computer-based exams available on demand. Students with no accounting background begin with FA1 and MA1.

courses.title: Recording Financial Transactions
courses.about: FA1 is the starting point of the route and assumes no prior accounting knowledge. It teaches how a business records its everyday financial transactions, from the documents it receives to the entries in its accounting records. It gives you the language and bookkeeping skills that every later accounting exam builds on.
courses.short: FA1 is the starting point of the route and assumes no prior accounting knowledge.
learn: How businesses and their accounting function work
Source documents and the books where transactions are first recorded
Recording sales, purchases, cash and bank transactions
Preparing and checking a trial balance
structure: Computer-based exam, available on demand
50 multiple-choice questions, 2 marks each, 100 marks in total
Duration: 2 hours
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Management Information
courses.about: MA1 introduces the way organisations collect and use cost information to plan, control and make decisions. It is the management accounting counterpart to FA1 and, like FA1, is designed for students who are new to the subject.
courses.short: MA1 introduces the way organisations collect and use cost information to plan, control and make decisions.
learn: The purpose of management information and who uses it
Classifying costs and understanding how they behave
Recording and accounting for materials, labour and overheads
Using cost information to support simple business decisions
structure: Computer-based exam, available on demand
50 multiple-choice questions, 2 marks each, 100 marks in total
Duration: 2 hours
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Maintaining Financial Records
courses.about: FA2 builds on FA1. It moves from recording individual transactions to maintaining a complete set of accounting records and producing financial statements. It suits students who have completed FA1 and students with some accounting background.
courses.short: FA2 builds on FA1.
learn: Receivables, payables and year-end adjustments such as accruals and prepayments
structure: Computer-based exam, available on demand
50 questions, 2 marks each, 100 marks in total
Question types: multiple choice, multiple response, multiple response matching and number entry
Duration: 2 hours
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Managing Costs and Finance
courses.about: MA2 builds on MA1. It looks at how organisations manage their costs, plan with budgets and raise the finance they need. It is the second management accounting step before the Diploma.
courses.short: MA2 builds on MA1.
learn: Budgeting and comparing actual results with plans
Sources of short-term and long-term finance
structure: Computer-based exam, available on demand
50 questions, 2 marks each, 100 marks in total
Question types: multiple choice, multiple response, multiple response matching and number entry
Duration: 2 hours
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Business and Technology
courses.about: Business and Technology gives you the big picture of how organisations work. It covers how businesses are structured, governed and controlled, how accounting and technology support them, and the standards of professional behaviour expected of accountants. It is the broadest and most descriptive of the three Diploma exams.
courses.short: Business and Technology gives you the big picture of how organisations work.
learn: How organisations are structured, run and governed
The role of the accounting function, systems and internal controls
How technology and information systems are used in business
Communication and personal effectiveness at work
structure: Computer-based exam, available on demand
100 marks, two compulsory sections
Section A: 46 objective test questions worth 76 marks
Section B: six multi-task questions worth 4 marks each (24 marks)
Duration: 2 hours
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.about: Financial Accounting takes you from double-entry bookkeeping through to complete financial statements and their interpretation. It is the foundation for Financial Reporting at the Applied Skills level.
courses.short: Financial Accounting takes you from double-entry bookkeeping through to complete financial statements and their interpretation.
learn: The accounting framework and double-entry bookkeeping
Ledgers, the trial balance and period-end adjustments
Preparing financial statements for sole traders and companies
structure: Computer-based exam, available on demand
100 marks, two compulsory sections
Section A: 35 objective test questions worth 70 marks
Section B: two multi-task questions worth 15 marks each (30 marks)
Duration: 2 hours
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Management Accounting
courses.about: Management Accounting teaches the techniques managers use to understand costs, set budgets and measure performance. It builds on the ideas introduced in MA1 and MA2 and prepares you for Performance Management at the next level.
courses.short: Management Accounting teaches the techniques managers use to understand costs, set budgets and measure performance.
learn: The nature and purpose of management accounting
Cost classification, behaviour and costing techniques
structure: Computer-based exam, available on demand
100 marks, two compulsory sections
Section A: 35 objective test questions worth 70 marks
Section B: three multi-task questions worth 10 marks each (30 marks)
Duration: 2 hours
Pass mark: 50%

levels.name: Skills Level (Applied Skills)
levels.description: A mix of objective test questions and written or calculated answers. LW is on demand; the other five exams are held in four sessions a year.

courses.title: Performance Management
courses.about: Performance Management builds on Management Accounting. It teaches how organisations plan, control and evaluate performance, and how managers use financial and non-financial information to make better decisions.
courses.short: Performance Management builds on Management Accounting.
learn: Specialist cost and management accounting techniques
Decision-making techniques, including relevant costing and the treatment of risk
Budgeting, standard costing and variance analysis
Control and the behavioural effects of performance systems
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: 15 objective test questions, 2 marks each (30 marks)
Section B: three objective test cases worth 10 marks each, five questions per case (30 marks)
Section C: two constructed response questions worth 20 marks each (40 marks)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Taxation
courses.about: Taxation teaches how tax applies to individuals, businesses and companies, and how to calculate and advise on tax liabilities. The exam is set in country-specific versions, so students study the tax rules of one jurisdiction.
courses.short: Taxation teaches how tax applies to individuals, businesses and companies, and how to calculate and advise on tax liabilities.
learn: Income tax on employment, self-employment and investment income
Tax administration and basic tax planning
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: 15 objective test questions, 2 marks each (30 marks)
Section B: three objective test cases worth 10 marks each, five questions per case (30 marks)
Section C: three constructed response questions, one worth 10 marks and two worth 15 marks each (40 marks)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Financial Reporting
courses.about: Financial Reporting teaches how to prepare financial statements under International Financial Reporting Standards, for single companies and for groups, and how to interpret them. It builds directly on FA and leads to Strategic Business Reporting.
courses.short: Financial Reporting teaches how to prepare financial statements under International Financial Reporting Standards, for single companies and for groups, and how to interpret them.
learn: Accounting for non-current assets, leases, provisions and financial instruments
Revenue recognition and other key standards
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: 15 objective test questions, 2 marks each (30 marks)
Section B: three objective test cases worth 10 marks each, five questions per case (30 marks)
Section C: two constructed response questions worth 20 marks each (40 marks)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Audit and Assurance
courses.about: Audit and Assurance introduces how audits are planned and carried out and how auditors report. It focuses on understanding risk, gathering evidence and behaving ethically, and prepares you for Advanced Audit and Assurance.
courses.short: Audit and Assurance introduces how audits are planned and carried out and how auditors report.
learn: The purpose and regulation of audit and assurance
Professional ethics and the auditor's responsibilities
Planning, risk assessment and internal control
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: three objective test cases worth 10 marks each (30 marks)
Section B: three constructed response scenarios, normally one worth 30 marks and two worth 20 marks each (70 marks)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Financial Management
courses.about: Financial Management teaches how organisations decide what to invest in, how to fund it and how to manage cash and risk. It is the quantitative finance paper of the Applied Skills level and leads to Advanced Financial Management.
courses.short: Financial Management teaches how organisations decide what to invest in, how to fund it and how to manage cash and risk.
learn: The role and objectives of financial management
Sources of business finance and the cost of capital
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: 15 objective test questions, 2 marks each (30 marks)
Section B: three objective test cases worth 10 marks each, five questions per case (30 marks)
Section C: two constructed response questions worth 20 marks each (40 marks)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Corporate and Business Law
courses.about: Corporate and Business Law gives accountants the legal knowledge they need to work safely in business. It explains the legal framework businesses operate in, how contracts and employment relationships work, and how companies are formed, run and brought to an end. It is offered in English and Global versions.
courses.short: Corporate and Business Law gives accountants the legal knowledge they need to work safely in business.
learn: The legal system and how law is made
Contract law and the law of agency
Forming and running companies, including the role of directors and shareholders
structure: Computer-based exam, available on demand for the English and Global versions
Duration: 2 hours, 100 marks, two compulsory sections
Section A: 45 objective test questions worth 70 marks
Section B: five multi-task questions worth 6 marks each (30 marks)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based exam, available on demand for the English and Global versions

levels.name: Professional Level (Strategic Professional)
levels.description: Two compulsory Essentials papers (SBL and SBR) followed by Options papers. Long scenario-based questions, four sessions a year.

courses.title: Strategic Business Leader
courses.about: Strategic Business Leader is the capstone leadership paper. It is a single integrated case study in which you advise as a senior professional on an organisation's strategy, governance, risk, leadership, technology and ethics. Marks are awarded for how you communicate and judge as well as for technical content.
courses.short: Strategic Business Leader is the capstone leadership paper.
learn: Strategy: analysing an organisation's position and choosing a course of action
Using financial and other information to support decisions
Professional skills: analysis, commercial acumen, communication, evaluation and scepticism
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
One integrated case study with three compulsory tasks
80 marks are for technical content and 20 marks for professional skills
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Strategic Business Reporting
courses.about: Strategic Business Reporting takes Financial Reporting to a professional level. You apply IFRS to complex transactions and group structures and explain the reporting effect and the ethical issues to stakeholders, so written explanation matters as much as calculation.
courses.short: Strategic Business Reporting takes Financial Reporting to a professional level.
learn: Group financial statements, including complex group structures
Applying IFRS to complex transactions such as financial instruments, leases and revenue
Professional judgement and the conceptual framework
Current developments in reporting, including sustainability
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: two compulsory questions worth 30 and 20 marks (50 marks)
Section B: two compulsory questions worth 25 marks each (50 marks)
4 marks are for professional skills
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Advanced Financial Management
courses.about: Advanced Financial Management is an applied decision-making paper for students who want a career in corporate finance, treasury or investment. It builds on Financial Management and tests both advanced calculations and the quality of your advice.
courses.short: Advanced Financial Management is an applied decision-making paper for students who want a career in corporate finance, treasury or investment.
learn: The economic environment and its effect on financial decisions
Treasury and advanced risk management, including hedging currency and interest-rate risk
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: one 50-mark case study
Section B: two 25-mark questions
20 marks are for professional skills (10 in Section A and 5 in each Section B question)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Advanced Taxation
courses.about: Advanced Taxation develops Taxation into tax planning and advice for individuals, owner-managed businesses and companies, including groups. Like TX, it is set in country-specific versions. Answers are judged on whether the advice is accurate, practical and clearly communicated.
courses.short: Advanced Taxation develops Taxation into tax planning and advice for individuals, owner-managed businesses and companies, including groups.
learn: Tax planning for individuals and business owners
Tax on transactions such as disposals, reorganisations and share transfers
Ethical and professional issues in giving tax advice
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: one 50-mark case study
Section B: two 25-mark questions
20 marks are for professional skills (10 in Section A and 5 in each Section B question)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

courses.title: Advanced Audit and Assurance
courses.about: Advanced Audit and Assurance develops Audit and Assurance into senior-level audit judgement. It assumes strong reporting knowledge from SBR, and ACCA recommends taking SBR first. Answers must be specific to the risk or scenario, not general lists.
courses.short: Advanced Audit and Assurance develops Audit and Assurance into senior-level audit judgement.
learn: Planning and risk assessment in more complex audits
Quality control, ethics and professional scepticism
Audit reports and other assurance engagements
structure: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, 100 marks, all questions compulsory
Section A: one 50-mark case study
Section B: two 25-mark questions
20 marks are for professional skills (10 in Section A and 5 in each Section B question)
Pass mark: 50%
courses.exam_format: Computer-based session exam (March, June, September and December)

programs.name: CA
programs.awarding_body: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP)
programs.tagline: Become a Chartered Accountant through ICAP — PRC, CAF and CFAP coaching under one roof.
programs.description: The Chartered Accountant (CA) qualification is awarded by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP). Students move through a series of exam stages and also complete practical training with an approved firm.

overview.title: How the CA qualification works
paragraphs: The Chartered Accountant (CA) qualification is awarded by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP). Students move through a series of exam stages and also complete practical training with an approved firm.
bullets: Qualifying Assessment Test (QAT): only for students with HSSC or A-Level results of 50% to 59%
Certificate in Accounting and Finance (CAF): eight papers in two groups
Certified Finance and Accounting Professional (CFAP): six papers
Strategic Case Study: a final integrated paper taken after CFAP
Practical training, hands-on courses and integrated modules alongside or after the exams

overview.title: QAT and Pre-Requisite Competencies (PRC)
paragraphs: PRC assesses the basic accounting, quantitative and business knowledge that the CAF stage builds on. Students can self-study or take classes with an ICAP-registered tutor. There is also a separate English Communication Skills course, assessed by the British Council.

overview.title: Certificate in Accounting and Finance (CAF)
paragraphs: CAF is the core professional stage. Its papers focus on applying technical knowledge and analysing business problems. The eight papers are split into two groups. Students can sit Group B papers after passing two Group A papers, and can sit up to four papers in one sitting.

overview.title: Certified Finance and Accounting Professional (CFAP)
paragraphs: CFAP is the final professional stage of the exams. It focuses on innovation and decision-making, using technical knowledge and analytical skills. Students must have passed or been exempted from all CAF papers, and must meet the training conditions, before sitting CFAP. Unless only one paper remains, students sit at least two papers in a sitting.

overview.title: Where students start
table: Register for PRC. QAT is not required.
Pass the QAT first, then register for PRC within 12 months.
Exempt from QAT. PRC exemption depends on whether the degree is in a relevant subject area.
Exemptions from PRC and some CAF papers, or the Graduate Conversion Course in place of CAF, depending on the university and degree.
Finalists of ACCA, CIMA, PIPFA or ICMAP
Exempt from PRC and specified CAF papers.
paragraphs: Exemption rules have detailed conditions, so students should always check ICAP's current rules.

overview.title: Strategic Case Study
paragraphs: The Strategic Case Study is the final paper. It tests integrated knowledge through one case study, and students receive pre-seen material 20 to 30 days before the exam. The paper is open book. It is offered twice a year (Summer and Winter), and students can sit it once they have passed all CFAP papers or have one paper remaining. It replaces MSA-2 Management Professional Competence.

overview.title: Hands-on courses and integrated modules
bullets: Before training or CFAP: Presentation and Personal Effectiveness (PPE) and MS Office for Business
Before CFAP-6 (recommended) and the Strategic Case Study (required): AI and Data Analytics
Before the Strategic Case Study: Governance and Ethics

levels.name: Qualifying Assessment Test (QAT)
levels.description: Only for students with HSSC or A-Level results of 50% to 59%.

courses.title: Qualifying Assessment Test
courses.about: The Qualifying Assessment Test checks basic English, mathematics and analytical reasoning. It is for students who finished HSSC or A-Levels with 50% to 59%. Students with 60% or more do not need it. Passing QAT lets you register for the Pre-Requisite Competencies (PRC) stage.
courses.short: The Qualifying Assessment Test checks basic English, mathematics and analytical reasoning.
structure: Computer-based test
Offered in March, June, September, November and December
Maximum of three attempts
After passing, you must register for PRC within 12 months, or retake the QAT
A model paper is available on ICAP's website

levels.name: Pre-Requisite Competencies (PRC)
levels.description: Three papers covering the basic accounting, quantitative and business knowledge that CAF builds on.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Accounting
courses.about: PRC-01 is the first accounting paper of the CA route and assumes no prior accounting knowledge. It teaches how transactions are recorded and how basic financial statements are produced, and it prepares you for Financial Accounting and Reporting at the CAF stage.
courses.short: PRC-01 is the first accounting paper of the CA route and assumes no prior accounting knowledge.
learn: The accounting equation and double-entry bookkeeping
Recording transactions in books and ledgers
The trial balance and period-end adjustments
structure: Assessments are offered every two months (January, March, May, July, September and November)
All three PRC assessments must be cleared within 15 months of your first attempt
Approved calculators are allowed
courses.exam_format: Assessments are offered every two months (January, March, May, July, September and November)

courses.title: Quantitative Analysis for Business
courses.about: PRC-02 covers the mathematics and statistics that accountants and business professionals use every day. It builds the numerical confidence needed for costing, finance and analysis at later stages.
courses.short: PRC-02 covers the mathematics and statistics that accountants and business professionals use every day.
learn: Mathematics used in business, such as percentages, ratios and financial mathematics
Using quantitative techniques to support business decisions
structure: Assessments are offered every two months (January, March, May, July, September and November)
All three PRC assessments must be cleared within 15 months of your first attempt
Approved calculators are allowed
courses.exam_format: Assessments are offered every two months (January, March, May, July, September and November)

courses.title: Business and Economic Insights
courses.about: PRC-03 introduces how businesses are organised and how they operate within the wider economy. It combines business studies with the principles of economics and gives context for the strategy, law and analysis papers that follow.
courses.short: PRC-03 introduces how businesses are organised and how they operate within the wider economy.
learn: How businesses are organised and managed
Principles of economics, including markets, demand and supply
Basic macroeconomic ideas such as growth, inflation and trade
structure: One paper of 120 minutes carrying 100 marks
Business and economics are assessed together in a single paper
Pass mark: 50%
Assessments are offered every two months (January, March, May, July, September and November)
All three PRC assessments must be cleared within 15 months of your first attempt
Approved calculators are allowed
courses.exam_format: One paper of 120 minutes carrying 100 marks

levels.name: Mandatory Hands-on Courses (HOC)
levels.description: Practical courses required alongside the exams.

courses.title: Presentation and Personal Effectiveness
courses.about: PPE is a mandatory hands-on course in the CA route. ICAP requires it to be completed before practical training or the CFAP stage. It is part of the Mandatory Hands-on Courses (HOC) offered at Leads College of Accountancy.
courses.short: PPE is a mandatory hands-on course in the CA route.

courses.title: MS Office
courses.about: MS Office for Business is a mandatory hands-on course in the CA route. ICAP requires it to be completed before practical training or the CFAP stage. It is part of the Mandatory Hands-on Courses (HOC) offered at Leads College of Accountancy.
courses.short: MS Office for Business is a mandatory hands-on course in the CA route.

courses.title: English Communication Skills
courses.about: English Communication Skills is a separate course in the CA route, assessed by the British Council. It is part of the Mandatory Hands-on Courses (HOC) offered at Leads College of Accountancy.
courses.short: English Communication Skills is a separate course in the CA route, assessed by the British Council.

levels.name: CAF Group A
levels.description: Core professional stage — Group A papers. Students can sit Group B after passing two Group A papers.

courses.title: Financial Accounting and Reporting
courses.about: CAF-1 is the core financial reporting paper of the CAF stage. It teaches you to apply International Financial Reporting Standards to real business transactions and to prepare financial statements. Questions mix short multiple-choice items with calculations, journal entries and written explanations.
courses.short: CAF-1 is the core financial reporting paper of the CAF stage.
learn: The Conceptual Framework for financial reporting
Property, plant and equipment, investment property and intangible assets
Impairment, borrowing costs and government grants
Statements of cash flows and changes in equity
Preparing statements of profit or loss and financial position
structure: Written exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time
Offered twice a year (Spring and Autumn)
All questions are compulsory
In the Spring 2026 paper there were nine questions in two sections
Section A: ten one-mark multiple-choice questions plus five written or calculation questions (50 marks)
Section B: three questions worth 15, 20 and 15 marks (50 marks)
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Taxation Principles and Compliance
courses.about: CAF-2 teaches how Pakistan's income tax and sales tax laws work in practice. You learn to compute tax liabilities for individuals, partnerships and companies, and to advise on filing, assessment and compliance.
courses.short: CAF-2 teaches how Pakistan's income tax and sales tax laws work in practice.
learn: Income Tax Ordinance, 2001: salary, business and other income, deductions and depreciation
Capital gains and the tax treatment of different taxpayers, including associations of persons and companies
Sales tax under the Sales Tax Act, 1990
structure: Written exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time
Offered twice a year (Spring and Autumn)
All questions are compulsory
In the Spring 2026 paper there were eight questions in two sections
Section A: six questions, including a multiple-choice question (66 marks)
Section B: two questions worth 17 marks each (34 marks)
Tax rates were provided on the last page of the paper
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Data, Systems and Risks
courses.about: CAF-3 is a new paper in the current scheme. It recognises how much modern accounting depends on technology and risk management. It covers how organisations use data and information systems, the risks those systems create, and how the risks are managed.
courses.short: CAF-3 is a new paper in the current scheme.
learn: The effect of technology on accounting and decision-making
structure: Written exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time
Offered twice a year (Spring and Autumn)
All questions are compulsory
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Business Law Dynamics
courses.about: CAF-4 gives accountants the legal knowledge they need to work in business. It combines the former Business Law and Company Law papers into one paper, so you study commercial law and company law together.
courses.short: CAF-4 gives accountants the legal knowledge they need to work in business.
learn: Company law, including formation, shares, directors and meetings
The legal responsibilities of directors and professionals
structure: Written exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time
Offered twice a year (Spring and Autumn)
All questions are compulsory
Pass mark: 50%

levels.name: CAF Group B
levels.description: Core professional stage — Group B papers.

courses.title: Management Accounting
courses.about: CAF-5 teaches how managers use cost and performance information to plan, control and make decisions. It was formerly called Cost and Management Accounting and is the first paper of Group B.
courses.short: CAF-5 teaches how managers use cost and performance information to plan, control and make decisions.
structure: Written exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time
Offered twice a year (Spring and Autumn)
All questions are compulsory
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Corporate Reporting
courses.about: CAF-6 takes financial reporting to the next level. It deals with more complex reporting issues and with the financial statements of groups of companies, and it builds on CAF-1. It replaces the former Financial Accounting and Reporting-II paper.
courses.short: CAF-6 takes financial reporting to the next level.
learn: Advanced IFRS requirements for complex transactions
structure: Written exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time
Offered twice a year (Spring and Autumn)
All questions are compulsory
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Business Insights and Analysis
courses.about: CAF-7 teaches you to analyse a business as a whole. You use financial and non-financial information to assess performance, understand strategy and support decisions. It replaces the former Managerial and Financial Analysis paper.
courses.short: CAF-7 teaches you to analyse a business as a whole.
structure: Written exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time
Offered twice a year (Spring and Autumn)
All questions are compulsory
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Audit and Assurance Essentials
courses.about: CAF-8 introduces how audits are planned and carried out and how auditors report. It is the main audit paper of the CAF stage and builds the knowledge you need for Audit, Assurance and Data at CFAP.
courses.short: CAF-8 introduces how audits are planned and carried out and how auditors report.
learn: The purpose and framework of audit and assurance
Professional ethics and the auditor's responsibilities
Audit planning, risk assessment and internal control
structure: Written exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 15 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time
Offered twice a year (Spring and Autumn)
All questions are compulsory
Pass mark: 50%

levels.name: CFAP
levels.description: Certified Finance and Accounting Professional — the final professional stage of the exams.

courses.title: Advanced Corporate Reporting
courses.about: CFAP-1 develops financial reporting to an advanced professional level. You work with complex transactions and group structures and explain your judgements clearly. It replaces Advanced Accounting and Financial Reporting.
courses.short: CFAP-1 develops financial reporting to an advanced professional level.
structure: Computer-based exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 30 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time and an extra 15 minutes allowed for computer-based delivery
Offered four times a year (Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter) from Summer 2026
Some papers are open book, and ICAP publishes the permitted books for each paper
Pass mark: 50%

courses.title: Corporate Laws and Governance
courses.about: CFAP-2 covers the corporate laws that apply to companies in Pakistan and the principles of good governance. It is aimed at the advisory and board-level issues a chartered accountant meets in practice.
courses.short: CFAP-2 covers the corporate laws that apply to companies in Pakistan and the principles of good governance.
learn: Compliance obligations of companies and their directors
Ethical and legal risks in corporate decision-making
structure: Computer-based exam, 100 marks
Duration: 3 hours 30 minutes, including 15 minutes of reading time and an extra 15 minutes allowed for computer-based delivery
